description: An independent space-tech initiative exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, engineering, and scientific innovation to solve real-world challenges in space exploration.
summary: Artemis astronauts will rehearse lunar south-pole operations at analog sites on Earth, but those sites are chosen by expert judgement and no one has measured which lunar terrain Earth cannot reproduce. I trained a convolutional autoencoder on 121,914 elevation patches from NASA's LOLA south-pole map and 27 Earth sites (NASADEM, ASTER), with no labels and no hint of which world each patch came from, then matched terrain across the two worlds. Judged against how often the Moon matches its own terrain, Earth is about half as good a source of lunar terrain (0.54×), falling to 0.02× for steep ridges and crater rims. Among Artemis III candidate regions, the most rim-rich are the hardest to rehearse: de Gerlache Rim is 9% matched, Haworth 40%. In Saudi Arabia, the Tuwayq escarpment ranks 8th of 27 sites, alongside Death Valley and Askja; the Rub' al Khali does not qualify. The method transfers directly to Mars.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

It measures how well terrain on Earth can stand in for terrain at the lunar south pole, and shows which lunar terrain Earth cannot supply. It ranks Earth sites as rehearsal locations and scores six Artemis III candidate landing regions by how much of their terrain Earth can reproduce.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Common grid: lunar and terrestrial elevation are resampled to 80 m per pixel. Earth data is smoothed to match LOLA's sharpness, chosen by measuring pixel-scale noise, so the model cannot separate the worlds by sensor differences.

2. Patches: everything is cut into 5.12 km squares (121,914 in total), with each square's tilt removed so only landform shape remains.

3. Model: a convolutional autoencoder (PyTorch) compresses each patch to a 64-number fingerprint and rebuilds it. It trains on equal Moon and Earth batches with rotations and flips, with 20 km regions held out for testing. No labels are used.

4. Terrain types: k-means groups the lunar fingerprints into four regimes, from gentle terrain to steep ridges and rims. The number was chosen for stability across data splits.

5. Matching: a lunar patch counts as matched when an Earth patch is as close in fingerprint space as the Moon's own terrain from another region. The Moon therefore sets the bar, and Earth is compared with it on equal-sized pools.

HOW IT WAS VALIDATED

- Physical measurements the model never saw (slope, roughness, and terrain enclosure under a 1.5° sun) test what it learned. Adding the fingerprint to slope statistics raises R² for predicting enclosure by 0.198 (95% CI 0.064–0.338); on the Moon alone, from 0.07 to 0.33.

- It ranks 7 established analog sites above 14 control and background sites with AUC 0.786 (permutation p = 0.022), against 0.643 for hand-built features. The result holds after adjusting for site size (AUC 0.72) and for a ±20% change in the match threshold.

- Plain slope statistics separate Moon from Earth better (AUC 0.981) than the fingerprint (0.952), so the difference it sees is real terrain, not an artefact.

RESULTS

- Earth is 0.54× as good a source of lunar terrain as the Moon itself: 0.70× for gentle terrain, 0.41×, 0.16× for basins, and 0.02× for ridges and crater rims.

- Artemis III candidate regions richest in rim terrain are hardest to rehearse: de Gerlache Rim 8.7% matched, Haworth 40.1%.

- Saudi Arabia: the Tuwayq escarpment ranks 8th of 27 sites and Asir 13th; Rub' al Khali and Wahbah rank below a flat control site.

BENEFITS AND GOALS

It gives Artemis analog planning a measured basis, and shows which terrain needs another approach, such as simulation. It also gives Saudi Arabia evidence for the Tuwayq escarpment as a lunar rehearsal site. The same pipeline applies to Mars: swap in NASA's MOLA elevation and retrain.

TOOLS

Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn, scikit-image, rasterio, pyproj, earthaccess, NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib. Trained on a MacBook. Web page: HTML, CSS and JavaScript on GitHub Pages.

LIMITATIONS

Topography only (no geology, composition or thermal data); 27 hand-picked Earth sites; 7 known analogs; a single training run; Artemis regions approximated by their named craters; Mars not yet run.
